checkpoint: Checkpoint: minimum budget to a target validation fidelity
author: Tomoya Hatanaka

slides.title: How much search budget a target fidelity actually needs
slides.lede: Answering last checkpoint's action item: two boundary runs, decided on validation only.

highlights.label: Known before:
highlights.text: physics-informed proposals beat random and greedy circuit search in all seven tested conditions; the closed-loop bonus was not general.

highlights.label: Measured now:
highlights.text: on the Ising chain the open loop meets the rule at budget 6 (12/12) while the closed loop does not (8/12); raising the XXZ budget from 8 to 10 moved the closed loop from 9/12 to 5/12.

highlights.label: Not claimed:
highlights.text: no single minimum budget, no interval, and nothing about the held-out test set, which was never evaluated in this work.

meta: Previous checkpoint: one-factor robustness stress test
New model calls: 138 · candidate circuits trained: 408
Measured cost at list price: USD 0.29 (hard cap USD 2.00, authorised in advance)
slides.next: The question, stated so that it can be answered.
slides.notes: The previous checkpoint ended on an action item rather than a result. This run executes it and reports two outcomes that are not flattering to the closed loop.

slides.title: What budget reaches a required accuracy, not which method wins
slides.lede: Every earlier comparison ranked methods at one fixed budget; that is not the operational question.
slides.text: For a target validation trash fidelity, what is the smallest candidate budget that reaches it in at least 10 of the same 12 paired seeds?

bullets.text: Claim under test (EXPERIMENT_CHECK_REQUIRED before this run): a budget below 8 suffices on the Ising chain, and the XXZ cell that fell one seed short at budget 8 is rescued by more budget.

bullets: Alternative that fits the same evidence (MODEL_INFERENCE): attainment counts near a threshold are dominated by run-to-run variation, so a budget change moves the count without moving the underlying fidelity distribution much.
Both were separable in advance, because each budget is run as its own independent policy rather than as a prefix of a larger run.
A result could exist under a false claim only if the counts were monotone in budget by construction. They are not: the runs are independent, so this was a genuine test.
slides.takeaway: The endpoint is a count of seeds over a fixed threshold, not a mean fidelity.
slides.next: What was already settled, and what this adds.
slides.notes: Stating the alternative first matters here, because the measured result turned out to favour it.

slides.title: Settled: semantics helps. Unsettled: how much search it needs

cards.heading: Settled (CONFIRMED, measured)
bullets: Physics-informed proposals beat non-semantic search in all seven previously tested conditions.
The result survives changes of budget, width, Hamiltonian and model.

cards.heading: Already shown fragile (measured)
bullets: The extra gain from a closed feedback loop is not general; it changes with every factor tested.
Invalid proposals become random draws, entangling validity with architecture quality.

cards.heading: The gap this run addresses
bullets: No budget between 4 and 8 had ever been run.
One cell sat exactly one seed short of the rule and had never been retried at a larger budget.

cards.heading: Novelty: recombined
bullets: The methods, prompts, trainer and seeds are unchanged; only the budget moves.
Closest prior work is this project's own previous checkpoint, reused here as controls.

side_cards.heading: Observed (measured)
bullets: Seeds at the target: 9 to 5 of 12.
Mean fidelity moved only -0.0076; 17 of 24 results sit within 0.01 of it.

side_cards.heading: Interpretation (inferred)
bullets: Near a threshold inside the distribution, the count is a knife-edge statistic.
Only the budget was varied, so no cause is isolated.

side_cards.heading: Not supported
bullets: That more budget harms the closed loop.
That the closed loop is generally worse.

slides.takeaway: Supports: the budget boundary is real and the count is threshold-sensitive. Does not support: any causal story about feedback.
slides.next: What would have to be true for this to be wrong.
slides.notes: Reporting the count faithfully matters more than explaining it; the mean shift is given so the reader can see the count is not a fidelity collapse.

slides.title: What bounds this result, and what is recorded but unresolved
slides.lede: Stated before any of it is used to argue for a next step.

cards.heading: What would overturn it
bullets: A repeat landing on the other side of the threshold; margins are thousandths wide.
A different target, which would reshuffle every count.

cards.heading: Validity range
bullets: 4 qubits, noiseless simulation, one circuit-capacity rule, one model snapshot, one XXZ anchor.
12 paired seeds; one open-loop pool shared across them, so 12 successes are not 12 generations.

cards.heading: Negative and null results kept
bullets: The closed loop fails the rule at budget 6.
The XXZ boundary probe did not rescue the cell.
Target 0.99: 0 of 12 everywhere, unresolved.

cards.heading: Left unresolved on purpose
bullets: 6 and 8 qubits and the alternative model were not probed; every method sits at 0-3 of 12 there.
A blind sweep cannot separate invalid generation from too little search or capacity.
Random fallbacks stay in the score: 12 of 408 evaluated candidates.

slides.flag: Attainment counts are not monotone in budget, so no statement of the form 'the minimum lies between X and Y' is supported by these runs.
slides.notes: The limits are deliberately stated before the recommendation.

slides.title: Spend more on resolution, or diagnose why 0.99 is out of reach
slides.lede: Both new cells are complete; the next move needs a decision, not more of the same.

conclusions.text: Ising chain, target 0.95: smallest verified passing budget is 6 for the open loop, 8 for the closed loop; budget 4 fails for both.

conclusions: XXZ chain, closed loop: no verified passing budget; 8 and 10 are both verified failures (measured).
Target 0.99 unresolved everywhere, both new cells included (null result).
New work: 138 model calls, USD 0.29 at list prices, under a USD 2.00 cap.

decisions.text: D1  Is the budget boundary worth more spend?
(a) repeat both cells with fresh generation seeds - turns a knife-edge count into a distribution
(b) stop refining; treat budget 6 open-loop as the working answer - free, but rests on one run
Recommended (a), Ising cell only; moderate confidence.
D2  What to do about the 0.99 target
(a) diagnose circuit capacity and training length instead of search
Recommended (a), moderate confidence; a budget sweep cannot separate the causes.
D3  Any confirmatory read of held-out data

next_steps.text: On D1(a): repeat the Ising budget-6 cell with fresh generation seeds; report both runs together.
On D2(a): write the capacity-versus-search protocol and its cost cap, then stop for review.
A yes to either commits to a new protocol document and a new cost cap before anything runs.
Already committed: report, raw logs with hashes, and the reproduction commands.
